title: A Radio Interview with a Young Chef
description: Four recordings about a young chef: a radio interview, a recipe, a chat between friends and a competition announcement.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · The interview
parts.intro: You will hear a radio presenter, Helen, interviewing a young chef called Nam.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Welcome back to Morning Kitchen. Today my guest is Nam Tran, who is only twenty-three and already owns his own restaurant. Nam, welcome.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Thanks, Helen. It's lovely to be here.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: So, did you always want to be a chef?

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Not at all! When I was at school, I wanted to be a pilot. But my grandmother had a small noodle stall, and I helped her every weekend from the age of ten. Slowly I fell in love with cooking.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: And then you studied at a catering college?

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Well, I started there, but I left after one year. I felt I was learning faster in real kitchens. I worked for three different restaurants before I opened my own.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: That sounds very brave. What was the hardest part?

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Honestly, the money. The kitchen was small and the cooker was secondhand. We opened with just four tables, and for the first month only my family came to eat.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: But now you're fully booked every weekend.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Yes, we're lucky. A local newspaper wrote about us last spring, and after that, everything changed.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: What advice would you give to young people who dream of a career in the kitchen?

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Be patient and be humble. You will wash a lot of dishes and peel a mountain of onions before anyone lets you near the stove. But if you love it, every tired evening is worth it.

parts.title: Part 2 · A quick recipe
parts.intro: You will hear Nam explaining how to cook a simple dinner.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Now, you asked me for an easy recipe, so let me share my favourite quick dinner, a lemon chicken rice bowl. It takes only twenty minutes.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: First, cut the chicken into small pieces. Many people use big pieces, but small ones cook faster and taste better with the sauce.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Next, make the sauce. Mix the juice of one lemon with two spoons of honey and a little soy sauce. Some people add chilli, but I prefer to keep it mild for my younger customers.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Heat a pan with a spoon of oil, and cook the chicken for about six minutes. Don't touch it too often. Let it turn golden on one side first.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: While the chicken is cooking, wash the rice and put it on the cooker. If you're in a hurry, you can use rice from yesterday, but fresh rice is much better.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Pour the sauce over the chicken in the last minute. It should become thick and sticky. Then serve it on the rice with some green onions and a few slices of cucumber.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: My top tip: always taste as you cook. Recipes are only a guide. Your tongue is the best teacher.

parts.title: Part 3 · After the programme
parts.intro: You will hear two friends, Linh and Ben, talking about the interview.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Did you hear the interview with that young chef this morning?

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: Only the end. Was it good?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Really good. He talked about his grandmother's noodle stall, and now I'm hungry. I'd love to try his restaurant.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: Where is it? Is it expensive?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: It's near the river, and the main dishes cost about twelve pounds. It's not cheap, but I think it's worth it for a special occasion.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: Well, it's your birthday next month. Why don't we go then?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: That's a lovely idea, but they're fully booked at weekends. My birthday is on a Saturday, so I might have to book weeks in advance.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: Then call them today. I'll pay for the dessert.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: You don't have to do that. Anyway, I'm not sure about the day. Perhaps Friday would be easier, because my brother works on Saturday.

script.speaker: Ben
script.text: Friday is fine with me. I'll tell the others.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Great. I'll phone the restaurant at lunchtime, when they're not so busy.

parts.title: Part 4 · A competition
parts.intro: You will hear Helen, the presenter, at the end of the programme.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Before we go, a few notes for Morning Kitchen listeners. This week we have a special competition.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: To enter, send us your favourite family recipe by email, together with a short story about why it's special. The closing date is next Friday.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: The winner will get a private cooking lesson with Nam in his restaurant kitchen for up to four people, plus a free lunch afterwards.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Please note that we can only accept recipes written in English or Vietnamese. Photos are welcome, but not necessary.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Last year we had over three hundred entries, and the winning recipe was a simple vegetable soup from a ten-year-old girl. So don't think you have to be an expert.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: If you miss the details, don't worry. You can find everything on our website, together with Nam's lemon chicken recipe, so you can try it at home this weekend.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: We'll announce the winner on this programme on Monday morning at eight. Now, here's the weather.
